title: Close fences the runner: no advance letter after a rejection, none before
acceptance: Pure fence: stopVerdict({ aborted:false, autonomy:'on', stageRead:'ranked', stageNow:'closed' }) -> { stop:true, reason:'moved', to:'closed' }; aborted:true -> reason 'canceled'; autonomy:'paused' -> reason 'paused'; stageNow === stageRead with no abort/pause -> { stop:false }.

Pure recipients rule: wrapUpRecipients over 3 submissions where sub A has a pipeline entry linked by dev_submission_id (promoted, advance) and sub B has one linked (promoted, held) -> only sub C's address is returned; a submission with no linked entry and an email-shaped contact is returned exactly once per address.

Close route, the everyday path: a lifecycle at 'promoted' whose posting has 2 submissions, one of them run through promoteSubmission (entry carries dev_submission_id) -> POST close writes exactly 1 'rejection' outbox row, addressed to the NON-promoted submitter, and answers notified:1 (today: 2 rows, the promoted candidate who was mailed 'Next step' is also told 'we won't be moving forward').

Orchestrator ranked stage: 3 evaluated submissions all above the floor, the lifecycle is closed (claimLifecycleClose) from the per-promote progress tick after the FIRST promotion -> runLifecycle returns stage 'closed', exactly 1 'invite' outbox row exists for the posting, exactly 1 pipeline entry carries this case's dev_case_id, and an audit row records the run stopping because the stage moved.

Orchestrator collecting drain: 3 unevaluated submissions, the lifecycle is closed from the progress tick after the first evaluation attempt -> the second and third are never attempted (1 tick total), stage stays 'closed', no 'evaluated' audit row is written.

Orchestrator approved stage: a lifecycle at 'approved' whose case already carries a frozen scenario, seed and baseline (no spawn), closed from the 'publishing' progress tick -> after runLifecycle no OPEN dev_postings row exists for the case, lifecycle.postingId stays null, and no pipeline entry was seeded for the case.

The postingId write after a mint is conditional on stage 'approved' (updateLifecycle expectedStage); when it matches no row the just-minted posting is set 'closed' and an audit row 'posting_withdrawn' names it - asserted by the source-shape pin in the fence test plus the approved-stage case above.

Regression: every existing devcase-orchestrator.test.ts case (tenant, language, pause mid-drain, cancel mid-drain, failing eval, terminal stage, freeze idempotence) and close/route.test.ts case still passes unchanged.
premise: app/_lib/db/devcase.ts:813 inserts every submission with status 'received' and app/_lib/db/devcase.ts:1299 is the only status UPDATE (to 'evaluated'); no writer anywhere sets a dev_submissions status of 'promoted' (grep over app/_lib for "dev_submissions SET status" returns only :1299).

app/api/devcase/lifecycle/[id]/close/route.ts:66 skips a submitter only when `submission.status === "promoted"` - a branch that can never be true - so :84-86 mails the 'we won't be moving forward' rejection to EVERY submitter with an address, including those the orchestrator promoted.

app/_lib/devcase-orchestrator.ts:531-563 mails the advance letter ('devcaseAdvance', kind 'invite') to a promoted submitter; messages/en.json:9808 closeConfirm promises the recruiter 'Non-promoted submitters get a wrap-up note'. The UI promise and the code disagree on the normal promoted -> closed path.

The promote link already exists: devcase-run.ts:1150 writes devSubmissionId onto the pipeline entry and app/_lib/db/pipeline.ts:2680 findEntryByDevSubmission is its reverse lookup (workspace-scoped) - the close route never consults it.

app/features/tools/devcases/DevLifecycleRow.tsx:49 offers Close for LIVE_STAGES, and app/features/tools/devcases/DevTypes.ts:395 LIVE_STAGES = published, collecting, ranked, promoted - so a human can close while the runner is mid-drain (collecting) or mid-promote (ranked).

app/_lib/devcase-orchestrator.ts:479-493 (ranked loop) and :411-421 (drain loop) re-check only signal.aborted and getAutonomy() per item; neither re-reads the lifecycle stage, so after a close the loop keeps calling promoteSubmission (:497, a board write) and sendComm (:548, an advance letter to someone the close just rejected). The stage mismatch is noticed only at :578 advance(), after every effect has fired.

app/_lib/devcase-orchestrator.ts:330-332 mints the live posting and then writes postingId with an UNCONDITIONAL updateLifecycle (no expectedStage), after up to three awaited LLM spawns (:203, :249, :294); :346-352 then seeds sourced candidates onto the board, all before :367 advance() can discover the stage moved. The close route's posting enumeration (close/route.ts:53-55) runs once at close time, so a posting minted after it stays open on a closed lifecycle.

app/_lib/db/devcase.ts:349-378 updateLifecycle already supports the compare-and-set (`AND stage = ?` when expectedStage is passed) and app/_lib/db/devcase.ts:1286 setPostingStatus exists - the fence needs no new store surface.
rollback: Seven files, one builder: the fence module and its test are new and imported only by the orchestrator and the close route, so `git revert` of the series restores the old loop checks and the old status test with no schema, catalog or API-shape change to unwind.
runner_up: Stage handlers as one typed table over LIFECYCLE_STAGES: retire the orchestrator's private STAGES copy (devcase-orchestrator.ts:68 duplicates devcase-transitions.ts:15) and fold the three copy-pasted freeze blocks (:201-326, llm / degraded / failed audit triple each) into one freezeArtifact helper.
body:
## Summary
The human close door and the autonomous lifecycle runner act on the same candidates, and neither sees the other. The close route rejects everyone because its promoted skip tests a status that nothing writes. The runner keeps promoting, mailing and publishing after a close, because its per-item stop check reads abort and pause but not the stage. This card adds one fence module that both sides consult at the moment of effect. The close then skips anyone the board already holds, and the runner stops before its next irreversible step once the stage has moved.

## Description
The concurrency-guards technique *preparation-is-the-staleness-window* says to re-read the authoritative state as the last statement before the irreversible step. The orchestrator re-reads `lc.stage` only inside `advance()`, and that call comes after the effects. In the ranked loop the effects are a board write and an advance letter. In the approved stage they are a live apply token plus a sourced board. The close route has the reverse defect: its skip rule for 'already has an outcome' (`status === "promoted"`) is a dead branch, while the real link (`pipeline_entries.dev_submission_id`, reverse-read by `findEntryByDevSubmission`) goes unused.

`devcase-lifecycle-fence.ts` is pure and has no imports. It holds two rules:
- `stopVerdict({aborted, autonomy, stageRead, stageNow})` is the ONE per-item stop decision. It replaces the two hand-copied abort/pause blocks in the drain and promote loops and adds the missing third reason, 'moved'.
- `wrapUpRecipients(submissions, entryFor)` is the ONE rule for who is owed a close note: anyone the board does not already hold, deduped by address.

The orchestrator calls stopVerdict (1) per drain item, (2) per promote item AND again immediately before `sendComm`, and (3) immediately before the posting mint and before sourcing. The postingId write becomes a compare-and-set on 'approved'. If that write loses, the posting just minted is closed again and audited as `posting_withdrawn`. The close route swaps its dead status test for `wrapUpRecipients`.

## Flow
1. The recruiter clicks Close on a row at `ranked` while the runner is promoting.
2. `claimLifecycleClose` flips the stage to closed. The close route mails only the submitters with no linked pipeline entry.
3. Before the runner's next promote, its re-read of `getLifecycle(id).stage` returns 'closed'. stopVerdict answers 'moved', the runner writes one audit row and returns. No further board write and no advance letter.
4. On the everyday path (`promoted` -> Close), the promoted and held candidates keep the one outcome they already have (the board, or the advance letter) and get no rejection after it.

## Expected impact
This closes a class of contradictory candidate letters. On today's normal close, every promoted candidate gets 'Next step' followed by 'we won't be moving forward'. On a mid-run close, candidates the close rejected are then told they advanced. It also stops a closed lifecycle from leaving an open apply token or a freshly sourced board behind. The stop rule moves from two hand-copied blocks to one tested function, so a fourth stop reason means a one-line change.

## Evaluation
Claim: the close door and the runner never produce two contradictory outcomes for one submitter, and no effect fires after a close.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass. Cases 1-2 have no module to test, cases 3-7 fail against today's code, and case 8 is the regression guard that the new behaviour must keep green.
After: 8 of 8.
Method: gate - node:test over devcase-lifecycle-fence.test.ts, devcase-orchestrator.test.ts and close/route.test.ts on the real throwaway DB (npm run test:unit), plus the challenge integration gate.
Result: pending build.
Gate: contract.
evidence:
grep -rn "dev_submissions SET status" app/_lib -> app/_lib/db/devcase.ts:1299 only (`status = 'evaluated'`); app/_lib/db/devcase.ts:813 `VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 'received', ...)`.
close/route.ts:66 `if (submission.status === "promoted") continue;` then :84 subject `Update on your submission — ${role}`, :86 `kind: "rejection"`.
messages/en.json:9808 closeConfirm: "Close this assignment? Non-promoted submitters get a wrap-up note and the apply link stops accepting submissions."
devcase-orchestrator.ts:479 `if (signal?.aborted) {` / :484 `if (getAutonomy() === "paused") {` / :497 `const result = promoteSubmission(s.id, floor);` / :548 `await sendComm({` / :578 `if (!advance({ stage: "promoted", detail })) return lostRace();` - no stage re-read between.
devcase-orchestrator.ts:330-332 `const posting = await getAdapter("local").publish(devCase); postingId = posting.id; updateLifecycle(id, { postingId });` - no expectedStage.
DevTypes.ts:395 `export const LIVE_STAGES = ["published", "collecting", "ranked", "promoted"] as const;` -> DevLifecycleRow.tsx:49 `const closable = (LIVE_STAGES ...).includes(lc.stage);`.
close/route.test.ts seeds only non-promoted submitters (:28-38), so the dead branch has never been exercised.
Not on the books: no leftover, digest or challenge-deck title covers the dead promoted skip or the runner/close race. The r06 devcase-session-api B card ('Close sees who is mid-case') covers in-flight SESSIONS and does not list close/route.ts in its write set. The open leftover 'Write close wrap-up notes through the comms translator' (devcase-lifecycle-api, M) is a different change (letter copy) and is not adopted here.

title: The lifecycle row reads a coded run outcome, and each warning offers its fix
acceptance: Vocabulary: STAGE_OUTCOME_CODES and OUTCOME_WARNING_CODES are literal arrays with derived unions. isOutcomeWarningCode('held') -> true, isOutcomeWarningCode('foo') -> false. parseStageOutcome of a stored JSON carrying an unknown warning code drops that warning instead of throwing.

Orchestrator ranked stage: a collecting lifecycle with one evaluated submission above the floor whose evaluation confidence is 0.2 (the low_confidence hold) -> after runLifecycle, getLifecycle(id).outcome deep-equals { code:'promoted', facts:{ promoted:1, topN:3, floor:<active floor> }, warnings:[{ code:'held', count:1 }] }.
Orchestrator collecting drain: two submissions whose evaluation throws (empty repoRef) -> the stored outcome carries warnings [{ code:'eval_failed', count:2 }] and facts.evaluated === 0.
Orchestrator halt: autonomy paused mid-drain after 1 evaluated -> outcome { code:'halted', facts:{ evaluated:1 }, warnings:[] }. A cancel gives code 'canceled'.

Pure actions: outcomeActions({ warnings:[{code:'held',count:2}] }, { caseId:'c1' }) -> [{ warning:'held', action:'open_decisions', href:'/?tab=decisions' }]. 'sourcing_failed' with a caseId -> action 're_source'. Outcome code 'halted' or 'canceled' -> action 'resume'. 'seed_skeleton_only', 'scenario_template_only' and 'baseline_unavailable' -> no action (explanation only).

Catalog parity: every STAGE_OUTCOME_CODES and OUTCOME_WARNING_CODES member has devcase.lifecycle.outcome.<code> in all four of messages/{en,cs,de,fr}.json. The test reads the catalogs, the same way devcase-vocabulary.test.ts does.

Legacy row: lifecycleDetailView({ outcome:null, detail:'published; sourced 3' }) -> { kind:'prose', text:'published; sourced 3' }. A row with an outcome -> { kind:'coded', ... }. Closed, redesigned and pre-migration rows keep rendering their detail.
Store round-trip: updateLifecycle(id, { outcome }) followed by getLifecycle(id).outcome deep-equals what was written. updateLifecycle without `outcome` leaves the stored one untouched.
premise: app/features/tools/devcases/DevLifecycleRow.tsx:212 renders `{lc.detail}` verbatim, and app/api/devcase/control/route.ts:73-74 serves the same `detail` to the control room.

Every orchestrator detail is composed English prose: app/_lib/devcase-orchestrator.ts:363-366 (published / sourced / skipped / sourcing failed), :448-449 (evaluated N, M failed), :576-577 (promoted N/3 (floor F), N held for review), :138 and :420 and :492 (halted), :411 and :482 (canceled). A cs/de/fr recruiter reads English on the row whatever their locale. The facts behind each string are integers the orchestrator already holds in locals (sourced, skipped, evaluated, failed, promoted, held, floor).

The row states problems without offering a fix. The only corrective action on it is Re-source, and DevLifecycleRow.tsx:154 shows it only after the 7-day stall rule (devcase-sla.ts:11 STALE_COLLECTING_DAYS = 7). A lifecycle whose sourcing CRASHED on publish (devcase-orchestrator.ts:353-358, audited `sourcing_failed`) waits a week for the button that fixes it.

Held submissions are the ones a human must act on (devcase-orchestrator.ts:523-530: 'still enters the pipeline for human triage'). The row reduces them to ', N held for review' prose with no route to them, although the Decisions deep link exists (`?tab=decisions`, app/features/shared/groupEvalArm.ts:3).

Degraded candidate materials are audited as distinct actions: `scenario_template_only` :218, `seed_skeleton_only` :264, `baseline_unavailable` :308. On the row they are only fragments inside a `detail` sentence, so a recruiter cannot tell at a glance that every candidate on the case got template probes.

dev_lifecycle has no structured outcome column (app/_lib/db/core.ts:798-812). updateLifecycle's patch (app/_lib/db/devcase.ts:351) accepts only `detail` as a free string, and app/features/tools/devcases/DevTypes.ts:171 types it `detail: string | null`.
rollback: One additive nullable column (ALTER TABLE dev_lifecycle ADD COLUMN outcome_json TEXT; old rows read null and fall back to prose) plus a new pure module and appended catalog keys. Reverting the commits leaves an unused NULL column, which SQLite tolerates, and the row reads `detail` exactly as before.
runner_up: Degraded-materials preflight: before the posting goes live, the approved stage surfaces a scenario/seed/baseline that fell back to templates as a human gate (publish anyway / redesign) instead of an after-the-fact audit row.
body:
## Summary
The lifecycle row is the operator's only window onto the most autonomous thing in the product, and it shows one English sentence. This card has the orchestrator write a coded outcome next to that sentence: a closed code, integer facts and coded warnings. The row renders the outcome in the reader's language, and every warning that has a fix carries it: held candidates open Decisions, a crashed sourcing offers Re-source now, a halt offers Resume.

## Description
The orchestrator already knows everything the row needs, as integers in its locals and as coded audit actions. It then flattens all of it into prose (`published; interview scenario degraded (template probes); sourced 0 candidate(s) before sourcing failed (...)`). The status-vocabulary technique *vocabulary-chain-integrity* is the fix: define the member set once as a closed type at the writer, then derive the stored token, the label catalog and the rendered presentation from it.

`devcase-stage-outcome.ts` holds the literal arrays STAGE_OUTCOME_CODES (collecting_open, awaiting_submissions, evaluated, promoted, halted, canceled, routed_to_human) and OUTCOME_WARNING_CODES (held, eval_failed, sourcing_failed, candidates_skipped, scenario_template_only, seed_skeleton_only, baseline_unavailable). The same module has their guards, a tolerant parser, `outcomeActions` (warning -> the action door that already exists) and `lifecycleDetailView` (coded vs legacy prose).

The orchestrator adds `outcome` beside every `detail` it writes. `detail` stays as it is, as the audit and back-compat prose. A nullable `outcome_json` column carries the outcome. The row renders a coded outcome as a localized line plus warning chips, and a row without one keeps today's prose. The existing Re-source handler, the Decisions deep link and the control route's reconcile are the only doors used, so no new route is added.

## Flow
1. The runner publishes. Sourcing crashes, and the seed falls back to a skeleton.
2. The row reads, in Czech for a cs recruiter: 'Published, 0 sourced' with a chip 'Sourcing failed - Re-source' (live now, not after 7 days) and an info chip 'Starter code is a skeleton only'.
3. Later the row reads 'Promoted 1 of 3 (floor 55)' with a chip '2 held for review' that opens Decisions.
4. The kill switch halts a drain. The row reads 'Paused after 1 evaluated', and the chip Resume posts reconcile.

## Expected impact
The operator stops reading English prose to find out what to do next: three blind states (held, crashed sourcing, halted) become one-click actions, and four locales see the run in their language. Because the vocabulary is closed and catalog-pinned, a new outcome the runner learns cannot ship as an unlabelled string.

## Evaluation
Claim: every outcome the runner writes is a closed code, rendered from the catalog, and each actionable warning maps to an existing door.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass (no module, no column, no outcome written).
After: 8 of 8.
Method: gate - node:test over devcase-stage-outcome.test.ts and devcase-orchestrator.test.ts on the real throwaway DB, catalog parity in the same test, plus npm run i18n:check and the challenge integration gate.
Result: pending build.
Gate: contract.
